feedback.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{-5{x}^{7}+1}{10{x}^{3}+x+3}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5{x}^{7}+1}{10{x}^{3}+x+3} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(-\frac{5{x}^{7}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{10{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{x}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(-5{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(10+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5{x}^{4}+0}{10+0+0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{4} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
